ingredients.item: Korean fish cake , any mix of sheets and tubes, sliced into bite pieces
toasted sesame oil , 1 tsp sesame seeds , 2 scallions cut into batons, a pinch of ground pepper

instructions.heading: Step 1
instructions.action: Oil and garlic at medium-high until the garlic barely blonds, onion and carrot in, 90 seconds of high-heat softening — the vegetables should stay crisp-shouldered, not slack.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the pan smells of toasted garlic and sweet onion; the edges of the onion go translucent while its core stays white.

instructions.heading: Step 2
instructions.action: Fish cake in, stirred 2 minutes — it will soften a touch, flex, and its cut edges will sear lightly where they touch the pan.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the fish cake's surface changes from glossy-oily to matte and it bends without breaking — it is ready to take the sauce.

instructions.heading: Step 3
instructions.action: Soy, corn syrup, gochugaru, and the splash of water in, tossed every 30 seconds for 2–3 minutes as the liquid reduces and glosses everything.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the pan is nearly dry with a glossy film on every piece, the fish cake's edges caramelized in spots, the gochugaru's color even across the bowl. Off the heat: sesame oil, scallions, sesame. The eating test — a piece straight from the pan — should be sweet-savory with the fish cake's distinctive bounce and the scallion still raw-bright.

storageNotes: Keeps 3 days refrigerated, honestly excellent cold in a lunchbox with rice; refresh in a pan for 90 seconds.
Variations: gochujang (a teaspoon) for the red-glaze fork; onion and jalapeño rounds for the drinking table; the same fish cake, unseasoned, into the soup pot with kelp stock is its other career.
